extracted.intended_audience: publishers, journal editors, authors, research administrators, and contributors who assign or report contributor roles for scholarly publications
extracted.subtask_description: Define and assign contributor roles for scholarly outputs using the 14-role CRediT (Contributor Role Taxonomy). The page lists each role with a short definition and notes about scope and usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and use of CRediT
rubrics_metrics.description: While CRediT is being used by publishers to capture information about the specific contributions of its authors, it is not designed to determine authorship; publishers adhere to strict guidelines around what qualifies as authorship. The CRediT roles can also be used to describe the contributions of individuals in contexts not related to article authorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRediT captures specific contributions but does not replace authorship guidelines; roles may be used beyond authorship contexts. Alongside each role definition the site includes examples of types of activity that may fall under the definition; these examples are illustrative and not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideas, formulation or evolution of overarching research goals and aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of types of activity may fall under this definition; examples provided on the source are illustrative and not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data curation
rubrics_metrics.description: Management activities to annotate (produce metadata), scrub data and maintain research data (including software code, where it is necessary for interpreting the data itself) for initial use and later re-use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes producing metadata, cleaning/scrubbing datasets, and maintaining data and necessary code for interpretation and reuse. Examples on the source are illustrative, not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Application of statistical, mathematical, computational, or other formal techniques to analyze or synthesize study data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers the use of formal quantitative/qualitative analysis methods; examples on the source are illustrative and not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquisition of the financial support for the project leading to this publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers activities related to obtaining project funding and grants; examples on the source are illustrative and not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Conducting a research and investigation process, specifically performing the experiments, or data/evidence collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encompasses hands-on experimental work or field/data collection; examples on the source are illustrative and not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Development or design of methodology; creation of models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes designing experimental, analytic, or computational methods and models; examples on the source are illustrative and not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Management and coordination responsibility for the research activity planning and execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers managerial, coordination, and administrative oversight tasks for the project; examples on the source are illustrative and not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of study materials, reagents, materials, patients, laboratory samples, animals, instrumentation, computing resources, or other analysis tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refers to supplying physical or computational resources necessary for the research; examples on the source are illustrative and not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software
rubrics_metrics.description: Programming, software development; designing computer programs; implementation of the computer code and supporting algorithms; testing of existing code components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers development, implementation, and testing of software and algorithms used in the work; examples on the source are illustrative and not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: Oversight and leadership responsibility for the research activity planning and execution, including mentorship external to the core team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes supervisory leadership and mentorship roles that guide the research project; examples on the source are illustrative and not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification, whether as a part of the activity or separate, of the overall replication/reproducibility of results/experiments and other research outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encompasses checking, reproducing, or otherwise verifying results and experiments; examples on the source are illustrative and not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation, creation and/or presentation of the published work, specifically visualization/data presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers creation of figures, visual representations, and data presentation for publication; examples on the source are illustrative and not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing – original draft
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation, creation and/or presentation of the published work, specifically writing the initial draft (including substantive translation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refers to drafting the initial manuscript or substantive translations; examples on the source are illustrative and not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing – review & editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation, creation and/or presentation of the published work by those from the original research group, specifically critical review, commentary or revision – including pre- or post-publication stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encompasses critical revision, commentary, and editing of manuscript drafts both before and after publication; examples on the source are illustrative and not exhaustive.
